title: Terminology Across Disciplines
text:
Specialists in different fields often rely on terminology that is nearly impenetrable to outsiders. A geneticist and a structural engineer may both speak of 'tolerance' or 'redundancy', yet these terms carry subtly different connotations in each discipline. Such lexical divergence is not merely ornamental; it reflects divergent epistemic priorities and the distinct problems each community has learned to solve. Consequently, interdisciplinary collaboration frequently begins with a negotiation over shared vocabulary.

Translators working between disciplines therefore face a delicate task, since a literal rendering can obscure the conceptual frame that gives a term its precision. Some scholars argue that the most effective glossaries document not only definitions but also the contexts in which a term acquires its authority. Without such contextual information, newcomers may adopt a word fluently in form while misunderstanding its implications. Ultimately, mastery of a specialized lexicon depends as much on recognizing these boundaries as on memorizing the words themselves.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, which term may both a geneticist and a structural engineer use?
According to the second paragraph, what can a literal rendering do to a term?
options: Obscure the conceptual frame that gives the term its precision
Remove all contextual information from it

questions.text: What can be inferred about newcomers who learn a specialized word without its context?
options: They may use the word correctly in form but misread its implications
They will quickly master the discipline
They will refuse to use any technical vocabulary
They will always translate the word more literally

questions.text: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Specialized vocabulary carries discipline-specific meanings that require context to understand
Scientific terminology should be simplified for the general public
Geneticists and engineers use identical terminology

vocabulary.definition: additional meanings or associations that a word carries
relating to knowledge and how it is acquired
lists of specialized terms with explanations
the vocabulary of a language or of a specialist field

paragraph_translations: Especialistas de diferentes áreas frequentemente recorrem a uma terminologia quase impenetrável para quem está de fora. Um geneticista e um engenheiro estrutural podem ambos falar de 'tolerância' ou 'redundância', mas esses termos carregam conotações sutilmente diferentes em cada disciplina. Essa divergência lexical não é meramente ornamental; ela reflete prioridades epistêmicas divergentes e os problemas distintos que cada comunidade aprendeu a resolver. Consequentemente, a colaboração interdisciplinar frequentemente começa com uma negociação sobre o vocabulário compartilhado.

Tradutores que atuam entre disciplinas enfrentam, portanto, uma tarefa delicada, pois uma tradução literal pode obscurecer o quadro conceitual que confere precisão a um termo. Alguns estudiosos argumentam que os glossários mais eficazes documentam não apenas as definições, mas também os contextos em que um termo adquire autoridade. Sem essas informações contextuais, iniciantes podem adotar uma palavra com fluência na forma, mas compreender mal suas implicações. Em última análise, o domínio de um léxico especializado depende tanto de reconhecer esses limites quanto de memorizar as próprias palavras.
